Theme

Household, washing & chores

tank noun

for water or other liquid

also water tank, tanks, vat, reservoir (tank)

classical

Cato Agr. 25 (Lewis & Short)
Verg. G. 4.173 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 390

lacus, lacūs m.

noun, fourth declension; dat. and abl. pl. lacubus

a vat, tank, basin

First any large vessel for liquids: the vat the wine ran into from the press, the smith’s tank for cooling hot metal; then a lake or pond (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • cisterna, cisternae f. — an underground tank for rainwater

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

    See cistern.

  • dōlium, dōliī n. — a very large jar, a vat

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 69.1 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. barrel: tank, vat

    The great earthenware jar for wine, oil or grain (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • aliī strīdentia tingunt aera lacū

    others dip the hissing bronze in the tankVerg. G. 4.172–173 (Lewis & Short)

See also cistern, barrel, fuel.
